NDT software in Phoenix: what the local inspection market actually looks like

Phoenix is not a refinery town, and that shapes the kind of NDT company that grows here. Arizona has no crude oil refineries; fuel reaches the Valley by pipeline from Texas and California. The inspection work that pays the bills comes from somewhere else: semiconductor fabs, power generation, aerospace, water infrastructure and a steady flow of structural steel for data centres, distribution warehouses and battery plants. The TSMC Arizona fab campus in north Phoenix and Intel's Ocotillo campus in Chandler have pulled in large volumes of stainless process piping, high-purity gas systems and structural steel. Palo Verde Generating Station, west of the city near Tonopah and operated by APS, is one of the largest nuclear plants in the country and runs refuelling outages on a fixed calendar. Honeywell Aerospace, Boeing's helicopter site in Mesa and Luke Air Force Base anchor an aerospace supply chain where penetrant, eddy current and ultrasonic work is routine.

Around those anchors sits the typical Phoenix NDT contractor: a small or mid-sized company running a mix of fab-shop weld inspection, structural special inspection on steel buildings, utility work for APS, SRP and gas distribution, and specialist crews that travel for outages or aerospace jobs. The regulators are part of daily life. Arizona is an NRC Agreement State, so industrial radiography is licensed through the Arizona Department of Health Services Bureau of Radiation Control; the NRC itself oversees Palo Verde; the Arizona Corporation Commission's Office of Pipeline Safety covers intrastate pipelines and gas distribution; and building departments across Maricopa County enforce IBC special inspection on structural welding.

Every one of those owners and regulators asks for the same thing in a different format: proof that a person with a current certificate used a calibrated instrument, followed an approved procedure and signed a traceable report. That is the job an NDT ERP does. The rest of this section walks through how the Atlantis ERP solution applies to Phoenix work, module by module, and what implementation looks like for a Valley contractor.

ERP for NDT companies in Phoenix: the short answer

An ERP for NDT companies in Phoenix is one system holding your technicians' certifications, your instruments' calibration status, your procedures, your job dispatch, your inspection reports and your quotes and invoices, all linked to each other. The Atlantis ERP solution is built for exactly that and is set up and supported by Atlantis NDT, whose founder is an ASNT NDT Level III.

The difference from a generic ERP or an accounting package is that the links are NDT-aware. A timesheet warns when the technician's certificate is not valid. A job assignment warns when the flaw detector attached to it is out of calibration. A report carries the procedure number, WPS, drawing and work order references, and moves through draft, in progress, review, approved and sent with inspector, reviewer and approver signatures. For a Phoenix shop running fab work in Tempe in the morning while an outage crew sits in Tonopah the same week, that linkage is what stops a paperwork slip from turning into a rejected report package.

Technician certification tracking software for Phoenix NDT crews

Technician certification tracking in the Atlantis ERP records every certification by scheme, level, method, certifying body, industry sector and issue, expiry and renewal dates, then computes status automatically: active, expiring soon (within 90 days), expired or revoked. Warning tasks and configurable daily email alerts go out before anything lapses.

Phoenix work makes that more than a filing exercise. Nuclear outage work brings owner-specific qualification requirements on top of an SNT-TC-1A or CP-189 written practice. Aerospace customers in Mesa, Tempe and Phoenix usually expect employer-based qualification to aerospace specifications, which you record under the 'other' scheme with its own certifying body and dates. Structural special inspection often needs a welding inspector credential alongside NDT levels. The certificate record holds all of that side by side, with OJT hours, training hours, exam results and scanned attachments.

Vision tests sit on the same record: Jaeger J1/J2 near vision, far vision, colour perception and contrast, with examiner, clinic, certificate file and expiry, and the same 90-day warning. The employee NDT profile adds highest level, methods certified, radiation safety training, radiation badge number and medical fitness expiry, so a radiographer's dosimetry badge and medical are visible next to their RT Level II before anyone dispatches them. Certificate templates per scheme set validity in months, whether a vision test or exam is required and the minimum OJT and training hours. See the Certificates app for the full field list.

Calibration management software that survives an Arizona summer

Calibration management in the Atlantis ERP tracks every instrument, probe and source-related item by serial number, with calibration frequency, status and next due date. A calibration certificate register holds the provider, certificate number, standard, range, uncertainty, accredited-lab flag and accreditation number, pass/fail/conditional result, the PDF and expiry alerts.

Heat and dust are hard on equipment in the Valley. A flaw detector left in a truck cab through a July afternoon, yoke cables baking on a roof deck, fine dust working into connectors on a pipeline right-of-way: all of it shows up as repairs. The maintenance log records preventive, corrective, repair, cleaning, firmware update and probe replacement events with condition before and after, so when a PAUT probe is replaced after a summer on girth welds, the history is there when the client auditor asks. Issue and return goes through supervisor and manager approval with condition recorded both ways, which settles the argument about who brought back the cracked UT cable.

Consumables get the same treatment: penetrant, developer, cleaner, magnetic particle baths, couplant and PPE, each with a reorder level, a low-stock flag and a movement ledger. Heat matters for PT in particular. ASME Section V limits the standard penetrant technique to surface temperatures between 40°F and 125°F, so summer work in the Valley often runs early in the day or under a separately qualified procedure, and knowing what stock you hold before a big fab job starts saves a trip across town. Details are on the Asset Management app page.

Crew dispatch and scheduling software for jobs from Buckeye to Queen Creek

Crew dispatch in the Atlantis ERP runs through Team Assignments: each job moves from planned to dispatched, in field, submitted and closed, with site GPS coordinates and mobilisation and demobilisation dates. Double-booking of technicians and of equipment serial numbers is blocked, and the system warns if assigned equipment is out of calibration.

The Phoenix metro is wide. A single week can include a fab site in north Phoenix, a warehouse steel package in the West Valley, a water treatment job for a city utility and an outage crew at Palo Verde. The technician availability calendar holds assigned, leave, training, sick and unavailable periods and blocks overlaps, and Time Off feeds straight into it. Each technician shows status, current assignment, utilisation and next available date, so a dispatcher can see who is actually free for a pre-dawn start on Thursday rather than guessing from a whiteboard. Calendar, kanban and list views cover the office, the yard and the phone.

Semiconductor and nuclear sites both run strict access rules. The Project app carries safety induction and work permit fields alongside client PO, contract, methods, codes, scope and acceptance criteria, so a technician without the site induction is visible before they drive out. If you move iridium-192 cameras around the Valley, the Fleet app records whether a vehicle can carry radioactive sources, its transport licence number and expiry, and which project and driver it is assigned to with dates and mileage. More in Team Assignments.

NDT reporting software for fab shops, fabs and outages

The NDT Reports module covers 17 report types, including UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ECT, PAUT, TOFD, UT thickness, PMI, hardness, ferrite, holiday/coating and computed radiography, each with its own numbering sequence and method-specific fields. Reports move through draft, in progress, review, approved and sent with signatures from inspector, reviewer, approver and, where needed, a third-party or authorized inspector.

That range fits the Phoenix mix. Stainless process piping on fab projects leans on VT, PT, RT and ferrite checks. Structural steel for data centres and warehouses means UT and MT on complete-joint-penetration and fillet welds, with weld lines carrying defect type and orientation and an overall result of acceptable, not acceptable or acceptable with remarks. Power and utility work adds UT thickness readings by direction, PAUT focal laws and TOFD. Aerospace suppliers need PT method and developer recorded properly, and eddy current reports of their own.

Clients who insist on their own report format are handled by versioned company templates in Excel, Word, PDF or HTML with your logo, header and footer; Excel templates fill automatically by mapping fields to cells. The offline field app is an installable web app that stores drafts and photos locally and syncs later, which matters inside fab buildings, underground vaults and steel-framed warehouses where the signal drops. See NDT Reports and the Digital Twin Reporting Software.

Procedure control for Valley contractors

The procedure register holds document number, revision, method, scope, material, applicable standard such as ASME Section V, acceptance criteria and either body text or an uploaded file. Procedures move from draft to submitted, reviewed, approved and published, with rejection reasons, locked approved revisions and a snapshot of every revision.

For a Phoenix company that matters when a nuclear or aerospace client audits you as a supplier and asks which revision of the PT procedure was in force on a given date. The AI-assisted first draft speeds up writing a new procedure for a method or material you have not covered before, but a Level III still reviews and approves it. Approvers get email notifications and reminders for pending approvals, so a procedure does not sit unsigned for three weeks while the job waits. Link: Procedures app.

NDT quoting and invoicing software for Phoenix contractors

Quotes in the Atlantis ERP carry job type, site, project dates and applicable codes, with NDT service products flagged by method and category, a global discount, a branded quotation PDF and online acceptance and signature that converts to a sales order. Invoices carry the NDT project, job or PO number, site, invoice type and industry sector, with subtotals for labour, equipment and consumables.

Invoice lines hold cost centre, method, equipment serial, technician, rate type and days or hours. Timesheets record work type (inspection, travel, standby, setup), method, billable flag, rate multiplier, site, client and equipment serial, with approval. That structure suits fab and outage work, where standby waiting for access or a permit is common and early-start or overtime shifts need a multiplier. Arizona charges transaction privilege tax rather than a conventional sales tax, and taxes are configured per jurisdiction during implementation. The financial dashboard shows revenue, cost of sales, gross margin, operating expenses, EBITDA, outstanding invoices, bills and expenses over a 12-month view. See Quotations and Invoicing.

Affordable, customizable ERP for inspection companies in Phoenix

The Atlantis ERP is positioned as affordable, accessible and fully customizable, with pricing given as a quote on request based on the modules and setup you need. Many Phoenix contractors start with certificates, asset and calibration management, dispatch and reporting, then add quoting, invoicing and CRM.

The CRM app suits a market where new fab, battery and data-centre projects keep appearing: leads carry service line, NDT service type, industry sector, site country and estimated technicians and days, with an NDT lead score from 0 to 100 banded hot, warm, nurture or cold. The Business Cards app turns a photo of a card from a trade event into a CRM lead in one step. The open REST API connects to QuickBooks, NetSuite, SAP, Maximo or any system that accepts API connections, scoped per implementation. For staff development, Atlantis offers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based training, an eLearning portal and the Practical NDT 3D simulator. To see it against your own jobs, book a demo for your Phoenix team.

Implementing the Atlantis ERP in Phoenix

Implementation is run remotely by Atlantis NDT with a Level III involved, so the people setting it up know what a calibration certificate or a written practice should look like. A typical sequence:

  1. Discovery: map your methods, clients, report formats, written practice and how dispatch works today.
  2. Data load: technicians, certifications, vision tests, instruments by serial, calibration certificates and consumables imported from your spreadsheets.
  3. Templates: your report and quotation layouts rebuilt as versioned templates, including client-specific Excel formats.
  4. Field rollout: the offline app installed on crew phones and tablets and tested on a live job.
  5. Go-live: alerts, approvals and dashboards switched on, with time-zone settings matched to Arizona, which does not observe daylight saving time.

Anything your Phoenix operation needs that is not a built-in feature is configured during implementation and scoped before work starts. Ask for an implementation quote.

Frequently asked questions

What is the best NDT software for a small NDT company in Phoenix?

The best fit is software that links certifications, calibration, dispatch, reports and invoicing in one place without a large IT team. The Atlantis ERP is built for that and can start with a few modules and grow.

Can the ERP hold nuclear and aerospace qualifications as well as SNT-TC-1A?

Yes. Certifications record the scheme (SNT-TC-1A, CP-189, ISO 9712, PCN, CSWIP or other), level, method, certifying body and sector, so client-specific qualifications sit next to your written-practice certifications.

Does the field app work where there is no signal?

Yes. The offline app stores drafts and photos on the device and syncs when a connection returns, with photo capture, on-screen signature and PDF preview.

Can it connect to QuickBooks or our client's system?

Yes. The open REST API integrates with QuickBooks, NetSuite, SAP, Maximo or any system that accepts API connections, scoped per implementation.

Does the ERP calculate inspection intervals or remaining life?

No. The ERP does not calculate inspection intervals. Thickness and remaining-life trends are visualised in the separate Atlantis Digital Twins product.

How much does the Atlantis ERP cost?

Pricing is a quote on request, based on your modules, users and setup. Request a quote for Phoenix.
